thread:
Evan: Quick ask — can someone run an onboarding bench for hera-7b-v1? Seeing slightly elevated p95 on longer prompts in canary. Need baseline numbers vs hyperion-7b. Sequence mix: 1024 (10%), 512 (30%), 128 (60%). Run both quant-4 and fp16. Target SLO: p95 < 220ms for 128 tokens on g5.2xlarge.

Maya: On it. Which runtime/build? And concurrency/batching settings?

Evan: Use runtime v1.12, g5.2xlarge, batching off (latency mode), concurrency=4. 1k samples per seq length.

Sam: I'll queue. @benchbot can you schedule warm and cold runs, plus a profiler sample?

benchbot: Scheduled job hb-20260317-01 for hera-7b-v1 on g5.2xlarge. Modes: warm/cold, fp16/quant-4, profiler sample. ETA ~30m.

Lina: quick note — last canary showed increased KV cache misses for long sequences. If you can include a warm vs cold comparison for 128 that helps triage.

Sam: Good call. I'll do warm/cold and add hyperion-7b baseline comparison.

benchbot: hb-20260317-01: warm fp16 complete. Summary (128 tokens): p50=42ms, p95=210ms, p99=340ms, tokens/sec=180. Artifacts: <https://redwood.internal/artifacts/hb-20260317-01|hb-20260317-01>

Evan: p95 210ms is inside SLO but p99 is high. Any OOMs or kernel fallbacks in the logs?

Sam: tail of GPU logs: ```
[INFO] GPU0 util=92% mem=12.1GB/24GB
[WARN] kernel_fallback: attention_cuda_kernel.cpp:72
[INFO] kv_cache_miss_rate=0.08
```

Lina: That kernel_fallback line is suspicious — looks like a suboptimal attention kernel kicked in for certain seq lengths. Might be a quantization+sequence combo. Try forcing the optimized kernel path with env RUNNER_FORCE_KERN=optimized.

Sam: Reran quant-4 warm with RUNNER_FORCE_KERN=optimized. benchbot reports: p50=48ms, p95=230ms, p99=360ms. p95 regressed slightly.

Evan: Hmm. So forcing that kernel didn't help for quant. @Maya can you run a quick NVTX-style profiler to see hotspots?

Maya: Kicking profiler now (short sample). Command I ran: ```bash
benchctl profile --job hb-20260317-01 --sample 60 --nvtx
``` Will post flamegraph.

benchbot: profiler job hb-prof-20260317-01 complete. Top hotspots: compute_attention_v2 (~43%), memcpy H2D/D2H (~17%), softmax_cuda (~9%). Artifact: <https://redwood.internal/profiles/hb-prof-20260317-01|profile>

Lina: Attention kernel dominates; memcpy is nontrivial too. I have a tiled-attention branch (tile-attn-try1) that reduces memory copies for long sequences. Sam can you run bench with that branch?

Sam: Spawning hb-20260317-02 with tile-attn-try1 (warm fp16 first).

benchbot: hb-20260317-02 (tile-attn-try1) warm fp16 summary: p50=40ms, p95=185ms, p99=290ms. :tada: Artifacts: <https://redwood.internal/artifacts/hb-20260317-02|hb-20260317-02>

Evan: Nice improvement on p95. Can we validate with cold cache and a throughput run (10k samples) to make sure no regressions under sustained load?

Sam: Queued cold runs + 10k throughput. ETA ~2h. Also will diff numbers vs hyperion baseline hb-baseline-20260310.

benchbot: hb-20260317-02 final: cold fp16 p95=205ms; throughput steady ~150 tokens/sec over 10k samples. Profile diff shows attention time down ~18%. Final artifacts: <https://redwood.internal/artifacts/hb-20260317-02-final|hb-20260317-02-final>

Maya: Attached profiler GIFs to the artifact bundle for review.

Lina: Action items: 1) Sam open PR with tile-attn-try1 + perf numbers, 2) I'll add a kernel-selection rule to prefer tiled-attn for seq>512, 3) Maya will upload profiler traces to the perf dashboard.

Sam: Opening PR now, will include bench artifacts and config diff.

Evan: Thanks team. Marking this thread resolved for the immediate SLO. We'll keep an eye during next canary. :white_check_mark:
